::: secret
**Relatives only.** If you are the explainer, close this tab. Part of your job is to find out what your relative cares about by listening.

**Play a real person, not a cartoon.** Aunt Dee has a real reason for this view. Be warm, a little skeptical, and human.

**The explainer will talk about Study Card B (the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine trial).** You can skim that card after the round, not before.

## Who you are

You're a nurse's aide at a care home. You worked through the worst of COVID-19 and you're proud of that. You got the vaccine because your job required it, not because you chose to, and that still bothers you. You felt pretty lousy for a day after the second dose.

## What you really care about

Being treated as someone who can make her own decisions. Your own health and your patients'.

## Opening line

> "They made that thing in a year. How can anyone know what it does long-term?"

## You must ask this (in your own words)

> "95% sounds made up. 95% of what?"

Notice whether the explainer can tell you where the 95% comes from using actual counts of people.

## Other things you might say

- "Nobody asked me. They just told me."
- "Of course Pfizer says it works."
- "I know people who got the shot and still got COVID."

## How you move

**Soften (open up a little) when:**

- you feel **heard**: they asked about your view and repeated it back fairly,
- they admit **uncertainty** or a real limitation honestly,
- they use an example from **your** life, or plain words and real numbers.

**Dig in (get more stubborn) when you hear:**

- jargon they don't explain,
- "just trust the science,"
- a condescending tone,
- "that's been debunked," with no explanation,
- a definition recited in textbook language.

You may ask **"What does that word mean?"** at any time.

**Move only as much as a real person would.** Partial movement counts as success. Don't give in just to be nice, and don't be impossible on purpose.

## After the round: your feedback

You go first. Tell the explainer:

1. Did they ask about my view **before** explaining? (yes / sort of / no)
2. Did I understand the **p-value or interval** explanation? (yes / sort of / no)
3. Did they name something the study **can't** tell us? (yes / no)
4. **One sentence that made me feel respected**, and **one word I didn't understand.**

Then say: *"Here's what moved me, and here's what made me dig in."*

## When the activity ends

Step out of the role: *"I'm not Aunt Dee. I'm ___."* On Zoom, rename yourself back.
